newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes soft on slight dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes soft on slight dlr demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed lower on late commercial demand for dollars, but sellers emerged and speculators disappeared and prevented the U.S. unit from making significant gains, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.70 to the dollar, after opening at 57.64. The rupee closed at 57.65 on Friday.

"There was some late import covering demand for dollars, which pushed up the (U.S.) currency," said a Deutsche Bank dealer. "But the dollar fell back when import covering finished, since there were plenty of sellers and a lack of speculators."
The exchange rate moved between 57.64 and 57.73 during the day, dealers said.
Overnight call money closed at 13.5 percent, after opening at 14 percent and rising earlier to 14.5 percent, as banks sourced two days of money since Tuesday is a holiday, dealers said.
Tuesday is Independence Day, which is a holiday in Sri Lanka.
